body: AWS launches AWS Interconnect - last mile preview with Megaport, a fully managed connectivity offering that allows customers to connect their branch offices, data centers, and remote locations to AWS with just a few clicks, eliminating the friction and complexity of network setup. As a milestone collaboration between AWS and Megaport, AWS Interconnect - last mile combines AWS cloud innovation with Megaport operating one of the world's largest Software Defined Networks (SDN), with 1,200+ enabled data centers across 31 countries. Through the AWS Management Console, customers can now instantly establish private, high-speed connections to AWS by simply choosing their preferred AWS Region, bandwidth speed, Direct Connect Gateway ID and partner subscriber ID. Once initiated, AWS generates an activation key to complete connectivity provisioning with Megaport. The launch simplifies the connectivity experience by pre-provisioning capacity and automating complex network configuration including BGP peering, VLAN configuration, and ASN assignment. At GA, customers will also be able to dynamically scale bandwidth from 1 Gbps to 100 Gbps through the AWS Console. The service is designed for high availability, with zero down-time maintenance, backed by a 99.99% SLA. AWS Interconnect - last mile is available in the San Jose (us-west-1) and N. Virginia (us-east-1) metros through Megaport. You can create a preview Interconnect using the AWS Management Console, Command Line Interface (CLI), or API. Partners can also easily adopt via a published open API package on GitHub . For more information, see the AWS Interconnect - last mile documentation and pricing pages .

title: AWS Batch now publishes job metrics to Amazon CloudWatch
body: AWS Batch now publishes job metrics to Amazon CloudWatch, providing native observability for batch workloads. AWS Batch emits metrics throughout the job lifecycle, giving you visibility into job queue health, failure rates, and job durations. AWS Batch automatically publishes job state transition and duration metrics to the AWS/Batch namespace in Amazon CloudWatch, with JobQueueName dimension. State transition metrics track how many jobs entered a given state, such as submitted, running, succeeded, or failed. Duration metrics track how long jobs spent between states, such as time from submission to runnable or total execution time. You can view these metrics in the AWS Batch console, the Amazon CloudWatch console, or through the AWS CLI and AWS SDKs. AWS Batch CloudWatch metrics are now published in all AWS Regions where AWS Batch is available. For more information, see CloudWatch Metrics page in the AWS Batch User Guide .

title: AWS Budgets now supports email verification for notification subscribers
body: AWS Budgets lets you set custom cost and usage thresholds and alerts you by email when your spending crosses the threshold. AWS Budgets now verifies new email subscribers before sending them budget alerts. When you add an email address to a budget notification, AWS Budgets sends a verification email to that address, and the address begins receiving notifications once the recipient confirms it. Verification applies to email addresses added from 9/30/26 onward. Addresses already subscribed on existing budgets are unaffected and need no action. For a new address, the recipient confirms it by following the link in the verification email, which opens the AWS Management Console. The AWS Budgets console shows the verification status of every subscriber, with a resend option for addresses still pending confirmation. AWS Budgets delivers these notifications through AWS User Notifications, and recipients can opt out at any time. AWS Budgets email verification is available in all AWS Regions, except the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions and the China Regions. To learn more, see Adding email recipients to a budget notification in the AWS Billing and Cost Management User Guide.

title: AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
body: AWS CloudFormation now makes it simpler to complete an update rollback and get back to deploying. An update rollback returns your stack to a known good state. Starting today, if some resources cannot roll back automatically, force rollback enables you to complete the rollback in a single operation. It works across every CloudFormation workflow, from the AWS CLI , and SDKs to AWS CDK and AI agents. With force rollback, CloudFormation completes the update rollback and returns your stack to a deployable state in a single operation, instead of requiring you to identify, list, and retry the operation for each affected resource. Any resource that still needs attention, such as one affected by a change outside CloudFormation, is recorded for you to review and resolve it before your next deployment. To get started, run continue update rollback with the force rollback option, then create a drift-aware change set to review any configuration differences before your next deployment. To learn more, see Continue rolling back an update in the AWS CloudFormation User Guide. Force rollback is available in all Regions at no additional cost. Refer to the AWS Region table for service availability details.

title: Launch AWS DevOps Agent to review findings and test results from AWS Resilience Hub
body: The next generation of AWS Resilience Hub now integrates with AWS DevOps agent allowing you to review failure mode assessment findings and implement mitigations to resolve findings and review resilience test results. AWS Resilience Hub is a central location in the AWS Management Console that helps platform engineering and site reliability teams assess and strengthen the resilience of their workloads running on AWS. It provides automated dependency discovery, generative AI-powered failure mode analysis, modular resilience policies, resilience testing, and organization-wide resilience posture reporting. Resilience test investigations: When you run a resilience test, Resilience Hub now launches an AWS DevOps Agent investigation that observes the test and returns a structured analysis. You can uncover symptoms, root cause, and impact along with observed recovery actions, like ARC Region switch. Interactive agent analysis from failure mode assessment findings: You can now start AWS DevOps Agent on demand task directly from a failure mode assessment finding in the Resilience Hub console, with the finding's context already in place. This allows for asking questions and investigating findings to create a mitigation plan. To get started, visit the AWS Resilience Hub console , select a service and configure DevOps agent in the service configuration. Then launch the DevOps agent directly from a failure mode assessment finding or a resilience test. To learn more, see the product page or visit the documentation . AWS Resilience Hub is available in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Europe (Ireland), Europe (London), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Paris), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Asia Pacific (Seoul), and South America (São Paulo).

title: AWS End User Messaging adds registration improvements for faster, higher-quality submissions
body: AWS End User Messaging now makes it easier to complete messaging registrations correctly the first time, with clearer guidance, explicit field requirements, and help avoiding the most common rejection reasons. Registrations ask for compliance evidence such as opt-in proof and sample messages, and submissions are often delayed or denied when that evidence is incomplete or a required field is missed. These improvements give you worked examples, surface exactly which fields you must provide, and walk you through the content that most often causes denials. First, example mock-ups of a compliant opt-in and sample messages are now included for US 10DLC, US short code, US toll-free and RCS registrations, so you can see what a compliant submission looks like before you build your own. Second, the registration API response now surfaces conditional logic, so you and your AI agents no longer have to guess which fields are required based on other field values. The response tells you which fields are required for your specific registration. Third, RCS registration now includes a walkthrough for recording the compliant video that agent registrations require. These improvements are available in all Regions where AWS End User Messaging registrations are available. To learn more and get started, see the End User Messaging User Guide .

title: AWS Health introduces the version catalog for software lifecycle management
body: Today, AWS Health introduces the version catalog which provides a centralized source of lifecycle information for software versions across AWS services. The version catalog helps customers move from reactive to proactive management of version upgrades and end-of-support risk. It is available in the AWS Health Dashboard, and customers on Business Support Plus, Enterprise Support, or Unified Operations can use the AWS Health API to integrate lifecycle data into their operational workflows. Customers running applications on AWS need to stay current with software versions to maintain a strong security and operational posture. AWS Health already sends account and resource-specific Planned Lifecycle Events well in advance for major version end-of-support milestones. The version catalog adds service-wide view of supported versions and their timelines, so customers can build upgrade schedules, governance controls, and move to newer supported versions before receiving an account-specific Planned Lifecycle Event. At launch, the version catalog covers multiple AWS services including Amazon RDS, Amazon EKS, and AWS Lambda with more services being added over time. The version catalog is available across all AWS Commercial Regions. To get started, visit the version catalog in the AWS Health Dashboard or read the documentation to learn more.

title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports cross-Region trusted identity propagation
body: Trusted identity propagation carries a user's identity with their request, so AWS services can grant permissions based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and log that user's access for auditing. With cross-Region support, this identity context can now be propagated to AWS services running in different AWS Regions, giving you greater flexibility in how you architect and deploy across AWS Regions. Customers often distribute workloads across AWS Regions for many reasons including separating the compute from the data it queries, to running workloads where capacity is available, or for disaster recovery and global scale. Previously, trusted identity propagation required all of the AWS services accessing a user's identity to reside in the same AWS Region. To reach services in another AWS Region, customers had to either grant access through broad IAM roles that cannot distinguish individual users or consolidate all their services into a single AWS Region. With cross-Region trusted identity propagation, a user's identity travels with the request across AWS Regions automatically, so you can grant access based on who the user is and their underlying group associations, and audit who accessed which resources, while preserving fine-grained access control for every individual user. Cross-Region trusted identity propagation is available at no additional cost in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. For the list of Regions where IAM Identity Center is available, see AWS Capabilities by Region. For more information, see Trusted identity propagation in the IAM Identity Center User Guide.

title: AWS Lambda durable functions increases durable operation and checkpoint payload limits
body: Starting today, AWS Lambda durable functions increases the maximum number of durable operations per execution from 3,000 to 30,000, and the maximum checkpoint payload size from 256 KB to 1 MB. Higher operation limits let you safely do more work in a single execution including expanding iterative loops, polling for longer time periods, and building more complex rollback paths that run when a step fails. At 1 MB, checkpoint payloads match the maximum payload size of asynchronous Lambda invocations, and integration services such as Amazon SQS, and Amazon EventBridge, so a workflow can persist a full event from any of these sources in a single operation. AWS Lambda durable functions helps you build resilient multi-step applications and AI workflows that execute for up to one year, with built-in checkpointing, automatic retries, and waits that suspend execution without incurring compute charges. Every durable operation counts toward the per-execution limit, including each step attempt, each poll of a wait-for-condition, and each branch of a parallel or map operation. With 30,000 operations, a single execution has more room to coordinate complex, multi-step workflows, iterate across thousands of items, or poll an external system for weeks, without exceeding checkpoint limits. An agentic application can reason over thousands of model and tool calls, and with 1 MB checkpoints it persists larger conversation histories, model responses, and outputs from tools directly in the checkpoint instead of writing to external storage. For state larger than 1 MB, the JavaScript and Python SDKs include a FileSystem serializer that writes the payload to an Amazon EFS or Amazon S3 Files mount and checkpoints a pointer instead. The new limits apply in all AWS Regions where AWS Lambda durable functions is available. To learn more about these service limits, see the AWS Lambda developer guide .

title: AWS License Manager now supports license type conversions for Ubuntu Pro purchased through AWS Marketplace
body: AWS License Manager now supports in-place upgrades for EC2 Ubuntu LTS (Long Term Support) instances to Ubuntu Pro available on AWS Marketplace. This allows customers to strengthen their security posture and meet compliance requirements without rebuilding their fleet or migrating workloads to a new instance or AMI. With an Ubuntu Pro subscription, customers receive security patches for up to 10 years — extendable to 15 years with the Legacy add-on. This coverage extends beyond the base OS to thousands of additional packages, including widely used open-source applications such as NGINX, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Redis. Ubuntu Pro also supports Kernel Livepatch, which applies critical kernel security fixes without rebooting to minimize downtime. With this launch, customers, who have an existing Canonical Ubuntu Pro subscription through AWS Marketplace, can upgrade directly during the conversion workflow. Customers who do not yet have a subscription can subscribe to Canonical Ubuntu Pro from within the AWS License Manager console. The new feature is available in all commercial regions where AWS License Manager is available. To get started, navigate to the AWS License Manager console and the AWS License Manager User Guide .

title: Improve your secrets security posture with actionable recommendations in the AWS Secrets Manager console
body: ​​​AWS Secrets Manager now integrates with the AWS Recommended Actions framework to surface contextual, actionable suggestions for your secrets directly in the Secrets Manager console. ​​ ​​With this launch, you can view tailored recommendations alongside your secrets to improve your security posture and follow best practices without leaving the console. For example, you can identify secrets that need rotation configured, use a customer managed key instead of default service-provided key for encryption, and act on secrets configuration improvements, all from a single view.​ ​​This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where AWS Secrets Manager is offered, at no additional cost. To get started, visit the AWS Secrets Manager console .​

title: AWS Transform announces Azure-to-AWS cloud-native code conversion
body: Today, AWS announced the general availability of application code conversion from Azure SDK to AWS SDK in AWS Transform, giving you an accelerated path to migrate Microsoft Azure cloud-native .NET applications to AWS. The AWS Transform .NET modernization agent identifies Azure service code and converts it to equivalent AWS service code. For example, an Azure Functions serverless function that uses Azure Cosmos DB can be converted to an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon DynamoDB. AWS Transform discovers the Azure SDK in your submitted source code and presents the conversion options in the assessment report and modernization plan. You can accept the options provided or adjust them based on your preferences before running the modernization. AWS Transform then converts the identified Azure service code to the equivalent AWS SDK calls, and validates that the changes are incorporated into the transformed code. The feature supports conversion of Azure Functions to AWS Lambda functions, Azure Blob Storage to Amazon S3, and Azure Queue Storage to Amazon SQS, with Azure Cosmos DB to Amazon DynamoDB conversion available in preview. AWS Transform is available in eight AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Tokyo, Seoul, Sydney), Canada (Central), and Europe (Frankfurt, London). To learn more, see Convert cloud-native code to AWS in the AWS Transform User Guide.

title: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now support 1:1 NAT
body: AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN now provide managed one-to-one network address translation (NAT) directly on their attachments, through integration with Regional Private NAT Gateway. This enables customers to connect private networks that share the same IP address ranges without renumbering either network, deploying a NAT appliance, or writing return-traffic rules. Networks with overlapping Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) blocks have long been unable to communicate, a common blocker during mergers and acquisitions, when connecting partner networks over AWS Site-to-Site VPN, in multicloud connectivity, and when independently provisioned VPCs need to interconnect. Using this capability, customers can define address-translation rules on a AWS Transit Gateway or AWS Cloud WAN attachment, specifying the private IP range each source CIDR translates to, across Amazon VPC, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, AWS Direct Connect, and SD-WAN appliances connected through Transit Gateway Connect. Both services apply translation automatically in both directions, with no separate return-traffic rule and no NAT appliance to deploy. AWS operates, scales, and manages the NAT capability as part of the attachment. For example, if a customer acquires a business and both VPCs use 10.0.0.0/16, they translate one VPC's addresses to a non-overlapping range on its attachment and connect the networks immediately. Customers set it up in minutes using the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), AWS SDKs, and AWS CloudFormation, and monitor translated traffic through Amazon CloudWatch metrics and Amazon EventBridge events. AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN offer 1:1 NAT through Regional Private NAT Gateway in all AWS commercial regions where they operate. For full pricing details, see Amazon VPC pricing . To learn more, see the AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN product pages, and the AWS Transit Gateway and AWS Cloud WAN documentation.

title: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening
body: Amazon Bedrock Advanced Prompt Optimization now supports prompt shortening, an optional setting that reduces the length of your prompt while maintaining or improving your evaluation scores. Advanced Prompt Optimization optimizes prompts for any model on Amazon Bedrock against your own evaluation criteria. Until now, optimization focused on quality alone. Optimized prompts were often longer than the original. Longer prompts raise input token costs and can increase time to first token, which matters at scale and in latency-sensitive applications. When you turn on prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset, the optimizer reduces the prompt's length. The optimized prompt is returned only when it is shorter than your original prompt and scores at least as high on your evaluation. Otherwise your original prompt is returned, so the setting never leaves you with a longer or lower-scoring prompt. Results include a compression ratio and the original and optimized token counts, in the output file and on the console results page. For example, a compression ratio of 0.7 means the optimized prompt uses 30% fewer tokens. Prompt shortening works with any evaluation method, including steering criteria, LLM-as-a-judge rubrics, and custom Lambda evaluators. Prompt shortening is available in all AWS Regions where Advanced Prompt Optimization is available. To get started, enable prompt shortening for a prompt template in your input dataset and create an optimization job as usual. To learn more, see Shorten prompts in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide, the Amazon Bedrock pricing page , and the Amazon Bedrock product page .

title: Bring deep SageMaker AI expertise to your coding agent with the AWS AI/ML skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS
body: Your coding agent can select, train, optimize and deploy models on Amazon SageMaker AI while working across the rest of your AWS environment in a single natural-language workflow. The AWS AI/ML skill is now a core skill in the Agent Toolkit for AWS , so it works alongside the toolkit's other AWS skills like EC2, Bedrock, and more. We released the new AWS AI/ML skill on the Agent Toolkit for AWS. The toolkit is now the single, supported integration point, replacing the previous AWS Labs skills and plugins, with a consistent and easy install and update path. The skill is also pre-installed into SageMaker Studio JupyterLab for use with Kiro or your coding agent of choice. Moreover, we extended the SageMaker AI capability areas supported by skills. Inference optimization : optimize deployed models for latency, throughput, and cost Model customization : end-to-end guided fine-tuning workflows, from use case definition through training, evaluation and deployment Serverful training for both traditional ML and generative AI MLflow: experiment tracking and model lifecycle management JumpStart model deployment and model recommendations: deploy pre-built JumpStart models and get guided recommendations on the right model for the use case Processing jobs: data preparation and ETL on managed compute The AWS AI/ML skill is available at no additional charge; you pay only for the AWS resources your agents use. To get started, install the skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS on GitHub, or use it pre-installed in SageMaker Studio JupyterLab. To learn more about using a coding assistant with your SageMaker AI workflows , see the Amazon SageMaker AI documentation.

title: Structured outputs for Claude models available on Amazon Bedrock
body: Amazon Bedrock now supports structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models across both the bedrock-runtime and the bedrock-mantle endpoint. Whether you call Claude through boto3 and the bedrock-runtime APIs or through the Messages API and the bedrock-mantle endpoint, you can now receive schema-compliant JSON responses that conform to a defined structure, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing. With structured outputs for Claude on Amazon Bedrock, you can automate reliable, schema-compliant tasks across industries. Examples include extracting every required field from financial earnings reports and compliance documents, parsing clinical notes into Electronic Health Records (EHR), and enriching product catalogs with consistent, validated results. You can also analyze contracts for key terms, parties, and obligations, or power intelligent support ticket routing where intents, sentiments, and entities always match your application's data model. To learn more, see the Amazon Bedrock documentation . Structured outputs is available where claude models are available. For more information check the regional availability details page.

title: Amazon CloudWatch announces log routing and chained log parsers
body: Amazon CloudWatch now supports conditional log routing and chained parsers via pipelines, giving you more control over how log data is transformed and which CloudWatch log group it's sent to. CloudWatch pipelines is a fully managed service that ingests, transforms, and routes telemetry to CloudWatch without managing infrastructure. Log pipelines often carry a mix of event types that belong in different places, and individual events can nest one log format inside another. With conditional log routing, you define routes that send each event to a different CloudWatch log group based on conditions evaluated against processed fields, so you can separate events by severity, source, or type and apply the right retention and access controls to each. With chained parsers, you can apply multiple parser processors in sequence, where later parsers consume fields produced by earlier ones. For example, you can parse a JSON envelope first, then apply a Grok parser to a field it extracts. Together, these capabilities let you structure diverse log formats and route them to the right log groups in a single pipeline. Conditional routing and chained parsers are available in all commercial AWS Regions where CloudWatch pipelines is generally available. You can configure these capabilities using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. To get started, see the Amazon CloudWatch pipelines documentation .

title: Amazon Connect Customer now lets you view metrics by customer lifetime value and repeat-caller status
body: Now you can view your metrics across customer segments: customer lifetime value (LTV) and repeat callers. See how any metric differs for repeat callers versus the rest of your contacts, or how results hold up among your highest-LTV customers; so you can spot the groups trending the wrong way before it shows up in the aggregate. Where a segment is underperforming, you can act. Route high-LTV customers to your most effective people, adjust the knowledge bases and self-service flows that repeat callers are falling back from, or refine agent guidance for segments where satisfaction is slipping. The segment tells you where to look; the metrics tell you what to fix.

title: Amazon Connect Customer now prefills step-by-step guides for after contact work
body: Amazon Connect Customer can now fill in the step-by-step guides that agents complete after a contact, using information extracted from customer conversations, such as booking identifiers, claim numbers, and conversation summaries. Managers can set which information populates each form field. Agents can review and submit rather than manually typing in each field, saving time and improving data accuracy during after contact work. Contact center agents spend time after each contact entering frequently used information into a step-by-step guide. For example, an insurance agent who finishes a claims call might record the customer’s policy number, a summary of the call, and a disposition code. Now, managers can define rules for which information to extract from the conversation and which fields to automatically fill in the guide. The agent can then check the information, make any necessary corrections, and submit the guide, shortening after contact work and reducing data entry errors. You can use step-by-step guides with information extraction in the following AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia), US West (Oregon), Asia Pacific (Seoul), Asia Pacific (Singapore), Asia Pacific (Sydney), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), Canada (Central), Europe (Frankfurt), and Europe (London). Contact summaries are also available in Africa (Cape Town). To learn more and get started, see step-by-step guides in the Amazon Connect Customer administrator guide.

title: AWS Deadline Cloud now helps users find their accessible resources in the Deadline Cloud monitor
body: AWS Deadline Cloud now lets users who have access to specific queues, fleets, or jobs, rather than an entire farm, find the resources they can reach directly from the Deadline Cloud monitor. Deadline Cloud is a fully managed service that helps teams run compute-intensive workloads for visual effects, animation, product design, simulation, and gaming. Previously, a user with access to only one queue had to get the farm ID from an administrator before they could reach their work. With this launch, the Deadline Cloud monitor displays to users queues they have access to, the parent IDs needed to reach them, and their level of access, covering both direct and group-inherited permissions. Teams now can share a single monitor entry point (URL) across different permission levels without additional coordination. Resource discovery is available in all AWS Regions where Deadline Cloud is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Deadline Cloud user guide .

title: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now supports Launch Before Terminate at account-level to replace instances
body: AWS EC2 Auto Scaling now lets you enable Launch Before Terminate as the default replacement behavior across all Auto Scaling groups in your account. When enabled, Auto Scaling launches a replacement instance and waits for it to pass health checks before terminating the instance it replaces, helping your applications maintain full capacity and availability during instance replacement events. This applies to replacement events such as instance refreshes, rebalancing, health checks, and maximum-instance-lifetime replacements. You can enable Launch Before Terminate through AWS EC2 Auto Scaling account settings, which let you configure the behavior once at the account level instead of on each Auto Scaling group individually. You can manage the setting with the new `PutAccountSetting` and `DescribeAccountSettings` APIs, available through the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or AWS SDKs. Launch Before Terminate is available in all AWS Regions at no additional cost. To learn more, see Launch Before Terminate in the AWS EC2 Auto Scaling User Guide and AWS EC2 Auto Scaling API Reference Guide .

title: Amazon ECS adds LiveTaskCount and removes the charge for RunningTaskCount metric
body: Today, Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) announces LiveTaskCount, a new ECS service metric that reports how many tasks are actively running in your service, available to all customers at no additional charge. Additionally, the existing RunningTaskCount metric in Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights no longer incurs a charge. LiveTaskCount reports the number of actively running ECS tasks across all desired states (ACTIVATING, RUNNING, and DEACTIVATING), including tasks still running while transitioning to a stopped state, for example, tasks undergoing connection draining during a scale-in event. This comprehensive state coverage makes LiveTaskCount well suited for autoscaling policies and capacity planning where a complete view of active, metric-generating tasks is required. It is available at no charge as part of ECS service utilization metrics and does not require opting in to CloudWatch Container Insights. The existing CloudWatch Container Insights RunningTaskCount metric tracks tasks where both the current and desired state are RUNNING, and continues to serve as a health and stability signal for customers who depend on it. With today's update, RunningTaskCount is now available at no additional charge for all CloudWatch Container Insights users. These updates are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECS is available. No action is required, and the pricing change for RunningTaskCount takes effect beginning October 1, 2026, and applies automatically. To learn more, see ECS CloudWatch metrics and ECS Container Insights metrics . For a pricing example, see Amazon CloudWatch pricing .

title: Serverless Storage on Amazon EMR Serverless now supports terabyte-scale shuffle
body: Amazon EMR Serverless now offers enhanced serverless storage capabilities with support for up to 1TB shuffle operations, raising the previous 200 GB per-job limit. Amazon EMR Serverless makes it simple for data engineers and data scientists to run open-source big data analytics frameworks without configuring, managing, and scaling clusters or servers. This enhancement enables enterprise customers to run production-scale Apache Spark workloads that require processing large volumes of shuffle data during complex operations such as joins, aggregations, and sorting. Enterprise data teams can now confidently migrate production workloads that routinely process terabyte-scale datasets without worrying about storage constraints. This enhancement is particularly valuable for workloads involving large table joins across multi-terabyte datasets, and complex aggregations on high-cardinality data that require extensive data shuffling. The addition of spill support ensures that jobs can seamlessly handle memory-intensive operations by offloading data to disk when necessary, improving job reliability and success rates for demanding analytical workloads. This feature is available with Amazon emr-7.14, emr-spark-8.1 and later, in 18 AWS Regions where Amazon EMR Serverless is available. See the Amazon EMR documentation for the full list of supported Regions and their applicable limits. To learn more about Amazon EMR Serverless and get started with terabyte-scale shuffle support, visit the Amazon EMR Serverless page .

title: Amazon GuardDuty RDS Protection now detects data exfiltration and destruction in Aurora and RDS databases
body: Amazon GuardDuty announces an expansion of RDS Protection that extends threat detection beyond login anomalies to identify data exfiltration and data destruction attacks targeting Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL databases. Available as RDS Protection for data activity, this new capability uses machine learning (ML)-based anomaly detection and integrated threat intelligence to continuously monitor database query patterns, helping you detect unusual data activity without requiring any agents, additional infrastructure, or database configuration changes. As attackers increasingly target databases to exfiltrate or destroy critical data after obtaining valid credentials through phishing, social engineering, or misconfiguration, their malicious database activity can appear indistinguishable from legitimate application behavior. RDS Protection for data activity establishes behavioral baselines for normal query patterns enabling GuardDuty to detect threats that traditional tools miss. You can enable GuardDuty RDS Protection for data activity as an add-on to RDS Protection for login activity. With a single click, they can enable it for their entire organization in the GuardDuty console, or programmatically via APIs, SDKs, CLI, or AWS CloudFormation. A 30-day free trial is available per account per Region. This feature is available today in all AWS commercial Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions, where Amazon GuardDuty RDS Protection is offered with support for Aurora PostgreSQL and Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. For supported versions visit GuardDuty RDS Protection documentation . To learn more and start your free trial, visit the Amazon GuardDuty product page .

title: AWS IAM Identity Center now supports optimistic locking for users and groups in its identity store
body: IAM Identity Center helps you configure the single sign-on experience of your workforce to AWS accounts and applications. You can now use optimistic locking for users and groups in the identity store, so that update and delete requests succeed only if the user or group hasn't changed since you last read it. This helps when multiple administrators or automated workflows modify the same user or group at nearly the same time, where previously one write could silently overwrite another. Each user and group now has a Revision value that changes every time the user's or group's attributes are modified, including through SCIM provisioning, Active Directory sync, or the IAM Identity Center console. Create, describe, update, and list operations return the current Revision, and you can pass it on a later UpdateUser, UpdateGroup, DeleteUser, or DeleteGroup request. The request succeeds only if the supplied Revision matches the current Revision. Otherwise, it returns a ConflictException, so your workflow can re-read the user or group and retry with the latest values. Providing a Revision is optional. Requests that omit it behave as before, so existing integrations continue to work without changes. Conditional requests are supported through the Identity Store API, not the SCIM endpoint. Group membership operations don't accept a Revision, and adding or removing members doesn't change the Revision of the user or the group. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where IAM Identity Center is available. IAM Identity Center is provided at no additional cost. To learn more about IAM Identity Center, visit the product detail page. To get started, see UpdateUser in the Identity Store API Reference .

title: Amazon Lightsail CDN distributions now support web application firewall
body: Amazon Lightsail CDN distributions now support integrated Web Application Firewall (WAF) capabilities, giving customers a simple, built-in way to protect their web applications. Previously, Lightsail distributions lacked native web application firewall capabilities, leaving customers without an easy-to-configure layer of protection. Lightsail now offers distribution plans with WAF capability at no additional cost. Lightsail's distribution plans can block common web exploits, malicious request patterns, traffic from anonymizing services (e.g. VPNs, proxies, and Tor nodes), SQL injection, OS-level attacks, PHP application-layer vulnerabilities, automated bot activity, and account takeover attempts. Once enabled, customers can monitor allowed and blocked requests through distribution metrics to maintain visibility into their site traffic. On the Lightsail console , you can enable WAF on the Security tab when you manage your distribution and monitor filtered requests on the Metrics tab. You can also enable WAF using the AWS Command Line Interface (CLI) or AWS SDKs. To learn more about enabling WAF for your Lightsail distributions, visit the Amazon Lightsail documentation .

title: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate mode
body: AWS Elemental MediaConnect Router now supports high bitrate modes with two new tiers: 250 Mbps and 500 Mbps. This allows professional broadcasters that need higher bitrates to transport high-value content without compromising quality or reliability. This enhancement enables industry-standard workflows such as VSF TR-07 compliant transport stream distribution for broadcast contribution, content distribution, and remote production. High bitrate mode supports up to two redundant sources for reliability and includes data plane optimizations that reduce jitter for improved performance. To learn more, visit the AWS Elemental MediaConnect product page and the MediaConnect pricing page .

title: AWS HealthOmics now supports shared VPCs
body: AWS HealthOmics now supports sharing VPCs across accounts, enabling your workflows to access resources in Amazon Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) managed by other AWS accounts with AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM). AWS HealthOmics is a HIPAA-eligible service that helps healthcare and life sciences customers accelerate scientific breakthroughs at scale with fully managed bioinformatics workflows. With shared VPCs, customers can centralize networking administration by sharing subnets and security groups from a single VPC across multiple accounts in their organization, and HealthOmics then places each account's workflows directly into those shared subnets. With cross-account VPC sharing, multiple accounts run inside one centrally managed VPC, instead of duplicating endpoints across VPCs. Workflows in participating accounts can access data privately without separate VPC peering connections or duplicated VPC endpoints. Previously, customers with centralized networking had to create separate AWS PrivateLink VPC endpoints in each VPC and maintain individual route tables using VPC peering. Cross-account VPC sharing reduces infrastructure overhead and simplifies network management for organizations with centralized networking while allowing researchers and developers to run bioinformatics workflows in their own accounts. Shared VPCs is available in all Regions where AWS HealthOmics is available: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London), Israel (Tel Aviv), and Asia Pacific (Singapore, Seoul, Tokyo). To get started, see the AWS HealthOmics User Guide .

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption
body: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports index-level encryption, letting you encrypt each index at rest with its own AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. This helps you protect data with different ownership or sensitivity under separate keys on the same domain. For example, you can encrypt each tenant's data with its own key in a multi-tenant application. Index-level encryption builds on the existing encryption at rest capability in Amazon OpenSearch Service. To enable it, set the encryption mode to Native and specify a customer managed AWS KMS key when you create a new domain using the AWS Management Console or the AWS CLI. You can then register additional keys with the domain and use them to encrypt individual indexes. Index-level encryption is available for domains running OpenSearch version 3.3 or later in 14 AWS Regions: US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Canada (Central), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Tokyo), Europe (Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Paris), and South America (São Paulo). There is no additional charge for the feature. Standard AWS KMS and OpenSearch Service charges apply. To get started, see Index-level encryption in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide.

title: AWS Partner Central launches Program Navigator, Case Study Generator, and streamlined specialization review
body: AWS Partner Central now features Program Navigator, a unified experience that lets partners discover, apply for, and track AWS Specialization program applications in one place. Partners can browse specialization designations, view requirements and benefits, and submit applications through a guided, step-by-step workflow. The new Case Study Generator in AWS Partner Central gives partners a redesigned creation experience with three starting paths: build a case study directly with AI assistance, import from an existing customer success story URL, or auto-populate from an opportunity. Case studies created for go-to-market purposes now follow a streamlined review path, a lightweight policy validation that lets partners publish directly to AWS domains without a specialization review. The deeper specialization-level review applies only to case studies associated with Program Navigator applications. Additionally, AWS has streamlined the specialization application review process through Program Navigator. Partners submitting applications can expect faster review times and more detailed, requirement-level feedback throughout the process. Partners applying for non-specialization programs continue to access those programs through the existing experience. Program Navigator and Case Study Generator are available to all AWS Partners in AWS Partner Central . To get started, navigate to Program Navigator and Case Studies under the Go to Market section in the left navigation panel.

title: Amazon RDS for SQL Server now supports snapshots on read replicas
body: Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for SQL Server now supports creating DB snapshots directly on read replica instances. Previously, you could create snapshots only on standalone and primary DB instances. You can now snapshot a read replica without promoting it first, giving you more flexibility in your backup and disaster recovery (DR) workflows. Previously, enabling Multi-AZ on a promoted read replica meant waiting for an initial full snapshot to finish before the conversion could begin. On larger storage configurations—such as io2 volumes up to 64 TiB—that first snapshot could take a long time, making DR timelines hard to predict. Now, Amazon RDS for SQL Server maintains snapshot data on the read replica throughout its lifecycle, so the first snapshot after promotion completes faster. This shortens the time to enable Multi-AZ and helps you plan DR exercises with more predictable recovery timelines. You can take manual snapshots of a read replica, turn on automated backups by setting a backup retention period greater than zero, and retain automated backups when you delete the replica; however, point-in-time recovery (PITR) from a read replica isn't supported. This feature works for both in-region and cross-region read replicas. It's available for SQL Server Enterprise Edition on all SQL Server versions that support read replicas, in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for SQL Server read replicas are available, including the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. To learn more, see Working with read replicas for Microsoft SQL Server . For pricing details, see Amazon RDS for SQL Server Pricing .

title: ARC Region switch adds four new capabilities
body: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) Region switch helps you orchestrate the failover of multi-Region applications to achieve a bounded recovery time during a Regional impairment. Today, Region switch adds four new capabilities: AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block, payloads for custom action Lambda execution block, service quota parity checks, and wait for target group health feature for compute scaling actions. AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block. During failover, you often need to run commands on managed instances and VMs. This execution block lets you invoke Run Command actions on managed instances during failover, with plan evaluation verifying that command documents target valid instances and that IAM permissions are correctly configured. Payloads for custom action Lambda execution block. ARC Region switch now lets you pass payloads to your custom action Lambda execution block, allowing reusability of your Lambda functions across recovery plans. Service quota checks. Service quota limits are a common failure mode during recovery. Region switch now verifies quota parity between your primary and standby Region, and automatically submits quota limit increases, reducing the risk of insufficient service quotas during recovery. Wait for target group health. Amazon ECS service scaling and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution blocks help you provision compute capacity during recovery, but provisioned capacity may not be ready to serve traffic. The optional wait for target group health feature verifies that your provisioned capacity is ready to serve traffic. To get started, see the documentation for AWS Systems Manager Run Command execution block , custom action Lambda execution block , Service quota checks and the Wait for target group health for Amazon ECS service scaling execution block and Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group execution block .

title: Amazon Route 53 now supports registrations, transfers, and renewals for Premium Domains
body: Amazon Route 53 Domains now supports Premium Domain Names. Customers can now search for, register, transfer, renew, and restore registry premium names directly through Route 53. Most domain registries set aside a selection of "premium" domains - names that are short, memorable, or in high demand. Previously, Route 53 Domains did not support these premium names, which meant customers who wanted them had to register and manage them through other registrars, fragmenting their portfolios across multiple providers. With this launch, customers can now discover and acquire premium domains directly in Route 53 Domains, consolidate their existing premium domains from other registrars, and manage premium and standard domains together through a single, unified experience. Finding and registering a premium domain works just like it does for standard domains. Premium domains appear automatically in domain search and availability results, with pricing shown upfront, so customers know the cost before they commit. To learn more about Amazon Route 53 Domains and start registering premium domains, visit the Amazon Route 53 Domains page . For a complete list of supported top-level domains, see the Route 53 TLD list .

title: Amazon SageMaker Studio simplifies getting started for new AI/ML builders with new sign-in options
body: Amazon SageMaker Studio now lets new customers sign up with their Google, GitHub, or Apple credentials and land inside a fully configured Studio environment - no traditional AWS account setup and no console navigation required. Previously, new customers who discovered a model on Hugging Face or an AWS product page had to complete a multi-step AWS account creation process, provide a credit card, navigate the AWS Console to find SageMaker AI, configure an environment, and set up IAM permissions before they could begin working. With earlier launches, we reduced environment setup to twenty seconds, pre-configured model customization permissions, and introduced deep links from Hugging Face and AWS product pages so customers could land directly inside Studio with a model pre-loaded. Now, with new sign-in options, customers complete a simplified sign-up using an existing identity, receive free credits as part of the AWS Free Tier with no credit card required in most cases, and arrive inside a ready-to-use SageMaker Studio environment where they can immediately fine-tune, evaluate, and deploy foundation models. Customers can invite team members by email, and collaborators sign in with their own email credentials to access the shared Studio environment, including shared models, notebooks, and endpoints without configuring IAM users or permissions. When a project grows beyond free credits, customers can upgrade to a paid plan and set a spend limit to stay within budget. Verified customers continue to receive default GPU access to G5, G6, G6e, and G4dn instances across endpoint deployments, training jobs, and notebooks without requesting quota increases. This feature is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Amazon SageMaker Studio is supported. To get started, visit any supported model on Hugging Face and select "Customize and Deploy on SageMaker AI" or "Deploy on SageMaker AI," or click Get Started from the SageMaker Studio page. To learn more, see the AWS sign-up documentation and SageMaker Studio setup guide .

title: AWS Security Hub now exports findings to S3 in CSV or JSON format
body: Today, AWS Security Hub announces support for exporting findings to Amazon S3 in CSV or JSON (OCSF) format. Security teams that need findings outside the console for use cases such as compliance reporting and audit evidence can now export findings from every findings page in the Security Hub console, including Threats, Exposure, Vulnerabilities, Posture Management, Sensitive Data, and All Findings, without building and maintaining their own extraction pipelines. With this launch, you can start an export on demand from the findings page you are viewing and have Security Hub deliver the results to an S3 bucket in your account. You can choose CSV when you want to review or share findings in a spreadsheet or export in JSON if you need these findings in Open Cybersecurity Schema Framework (OCSF) format. Findings export is available in all AWS Regions where AWS Security Hub is available. To learn more, visit the AWS Security Hub User Guide at https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/securityhub-v2-findings-export.html .

title: AWS Partner Central adds Solution Matching Engine performance insights
body: AWS Partner Central now gives AWS Partners more visibility into how the Solution Matching Engine (SME) contributes to their co-sell pipeline. The Solution Matching Engine performance section in Partner Analytics helps partners understand how SME performs for their company and AWS Marketplace listings. Partners can view recommendations, SME-attributed opportunities, their share of AWS-originated opportunities, stall rate, and pipeline attributed to SME. They can filter by recommendation type or AWS Marketplace listing and explore top customer profiles by Region, industry, and segment. These insights help partners assess their visibility and decide where to improve their listings and opportunity information. All partners eligible for APN Customer Engagements (ACE) can find the section on the Opportunity pipeline analysis page under Partner Analytics in AWS Partner Central . To learn more about SME and how to strengthen your visibility with AWS sellers, read Solution Matching Engine: Your Gateway to AWS Sellers .

title: Amazon Time Sync Service adds support for microsecond-accurate time on 135 additional EC2 instance types in all commercial regions
body: Amazon Time Sync Service introduces support for microsecond-accurate time on 135 additional EC2 instance types—spanning 12 instance families—in all commercial regions. Built on Amazon's proven network infrastructure and the AWS Nitro System, microsecond-accurate time and nanosecond-precision hardware timestamps leverage the reference clocks running in the Nitro System directly, enabling customers to easily order application events, measure 1-way network latency, and increase distributed application transaction speed. The newly supported families include eight Gen8 families (C8a, C8i, C8i-flex, C8id, M8i, M8i-flex, R8a, and X8i) and four Gen9 families (C9g, C9gd, M9g, and M9gd). Starting today, customers can access microsecond-accurate time on these additional instance types by creating a Precision Time Placement Group (PTPG), a new placement strategy that allows customers to launch instances with Precision Time Protocol hardware clock (PHC) enabled. Customers that require both low network latency as well as precision time can associate a PTPG with their Cluster Placement Group (CPG), so that their low-latency workloads also benefit from microsecond-accurate time. For more information, refer to the Amazon Time Sync Service documentation .

title: AWS Transfer Family supports custom ports for public SFTP servers
body: AWS Transfer Family now lets you configure custom ports on public SFTP servers and choose a communication mode for each port. You can support clients that require different ports or start SFTP connections differently on a single server. Previously, public SFTP servers accepted connections only on port 22 and used server-first communication. With this launch, you can configure up to three ports (22, or any port from 2000 to 65535), allowing you to use the port numbers your business or network requires and offer multiple ports on one server. Some SFTP clients initiate communication themselves, and their connections can occasionally stall on a server-first port. For each port, you can now select client-first or server-first communication and direct clients to the port that matches their connection behavior. Using a port other than 22 can also reduce unwanted connection attempts from automated scanners that target port 22. This capability is available in all AWS Regions where Transfer Family public SFTP servers are offered. To get started, visit the AWS Transfer Family console or use the AWS CLI or AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit Create an SFTP-enabled server in the AWS Transfer Family User Guide

title: AWS Transform adds storage migration assessments for Amazon S3, EBS, EFS, and FSx
body: Migration assessments in AWS Transform now evaluate on-premises storage for migration to AWS. Instead of manually analyzing thousands of volumes across protocols, capacity, and performance, you upload a storage inventory and AWS Transform does the mapping for you. It matches each workload to the best-fit service, sizes the recommendation, and projects costs to produce a total cost of ownership business case. Bring NAS shares, SAN LUNs, direct-attached disks, or backup repositories via a NetApp Digital Advisor export, RVTools file, or other inventory. AWS Transform routes workloads across Amazon S3, Amazon EBS, Amazon EFS, and Amazon FSx (NetApp ONTAP, Windows File Server, OpenZFS, Lustre). Run what-if scenarios to compare deployment options such as Single-AZ vs. Multi-AZ or cost-optimized vs. performance-optimized, then ask follow-up questions about any result in chat. Storage migration assessments are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is available. To learn more, see the AWS Transform User Guide .

title: Amazon MSK now supports configuring custom domain names for MSK Provisioned clusters
body: You can now easily configure custom domain names on Amazon MSK Provisioned clusters, on either ZooKeeper or KRaft mode for metadata management. This capability helps client applications maintain the same connection endpoints, simplifying cluster migrations, disaster recovery failovers, and scaling operations without reconfiguration. Previously, customers configured custom domain names manually on each broker. Additionally, on KRaft-based clusters, customers could not configure custom domain names. With this launch, you can now easily define a custom domain once at the cluster level, and Amazon MSK automatically applies it to every broker in the cluster, eliminating the need to configure each broker individually. The configuration persists through scaling operations and works identically on both ZooKeeper and KRaft-based clusters. This is particularly useful for customers who route traffic through Network Load Balancers, require persistent endpoints across cluster operations, or must adhere to organizational naming conventions for security and compliance. You can configure custom domain names on all new and existing MSK Provisioned clusters, in all AWS Regions where Amazon MSK Provisioned is available, at no additional cost. To learn more, see the Amazon MSK Developer Guide .

title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports Graviton4 based i8ge instances
body: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports i8ge instances, which is the latest generation of storage optimized instances offering the best performance for storage-intensive workloads. Powered by AWS Graviton4 processors, I8ge instances deliver up to 60% better compute performance compared to previous generation Graviton2-based storage optimized Im4gn instances. I8ge instances use the latest third generation AWS Nitro SSDs, local NVMe storage that deliver up to 55% better real-time storage performance per TB while offering up to 60% lower storage I/O latency and up to 75% lower storage I/O latency variability compared to previous generation Im4gn instances. Built on the AWS Nitro System , these instances oﬄoad CPU virtualization, storage, and networking functions to dedicated hardware and software enhancing the performance and security for your workloads. I8ge instances are available of sizes up to 18xlarge and 45 TB instance storage. At 112.5 Gbps, these instances have the highest networking bandwidth among storage optimized instances available in Amazon OpenSearch Service. I8ge instances support all OpenSearch versions & Elasticsearch (open source) versions 7.9 and 7.10. Amazon OpenSearch Service supports i8ge instances in following AWS Regions : US East (N. Virginia), US East (Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland), Europe (Stockholm), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Mumbai), Asia Pacific (Singapore) and Asia Pacific (Sydney). For region specific availability & pricing, visit our pricing page . To learn more about Amazon OpenSearch Service and its capabilities, visit our product page .

title: AWS AppConfig launches managed experimentation tools for A/B testing
body: Today, AWS announces the general availability of experimentation tools in AWS AppConfig, a new capability that enables you to run A/B tests and feature experiments without building or managing separate experimentation infrastructure. Built on 25+ years of Amazon experimentation best practices, AWS AppConfig experimentation tools use AI-driven guidance to help you build robust experiments while providing exposure control and locked treatment allocations so you can make confident, data-driven decisions about what to ship to your customers. Using AWS AppConfig experimentation tools, you can run A/B tests and multivariate experiments across your application stack, from UI changes and recommendation algorithms to AI model selections and prompt experiments. Define feature variations, target granular audiences using a rule builder, and set traffic allocation percentages through the AWS Management Console, CLI, API, or AWS CDK. AI-assisted experiment design can validate your setup against Amazon's best practices, helping you build experiments with sufficient statistical power. Customers set up and run the experiment in AWS AppConfig, and then analyze results using Amazon CloudWatch or existing analytics tools. At the end of the experiment, you promote the winning treatment to production through a standard AWS AppConfig safe rollout. Experiments work across workloads on Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, and on-premises servers through AWS AppConfig Agent.

title: AWS Transform continuous modernization is now generally available
body: AWS Transform continuous modernization is now generally available in all AWS Regions where AWS Transform is supported . This capability helps engineering teams analyze and remediate technical debt across source code repositories at scale. Teams can connect GitHub organizations, GitLab groups, and Bitbucket workspaces, run analyses on demand or on a recurring schedule, and prioritize findings across technical debt, security, agentic readiness, modernization readiness, and custom analysis criteria. With today's launch, you can connect source code providers, initiate and schedule analyses, review findings, and create remediations directly from the AWS Transform web application. For findings with an associated remediation, continuous modernization creates branches and opens pull requests or merge requests containing validated code changes for review. Analysis and remediation run in your AWS account using your credentials, while your source code remains under your control. You can also use the AWS Transform Kiro Power, agent plugins, or AWS Transform CLI to work from your IDE or terminal, analyze local repositories, organize repositories using labels, and run analyses locally or remotely using Amazon EC2 or AWS Batch. To get started, open the AWS Transform web application or use the AWS Transform Kiro Power and agent plugins . To learn more, see AWS Transform continuous modernization in the AWS Transform User Guide.

title: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) now supports prepared statements in Logged Batches
body: Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) now supports prepared statements within logged batches, so you can combine the atomicity guarantees of logged batches with the performance and efficiency of prepared statements. You can group multiple prepared INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements into a single atomic batch, where either all operations succeed or none of them do, while reducing query parsing overhead for repeated multi-statement writes. Amazon Keyspaces is a scalable, highly available, and managed Apache Cassandra-compatible database service. Because Amazon Keyspaces is serverless, you pay for only the resources that you use, and you can build applications that serve thousands of requests per second with virtually unlimited throughput and storage. Prepared statements let you define the structure of a Cassandra Query Language (CQL) statement once and run it repeatedly with different values, which improves performance and reduces overhead for frequently executed queries. With prepared statement support in logged batches, you can build atomic multi-statement operations that are both consistent and efficient, using the same CQL statements that you already use. Prepared statements in logged batches are available in all commercial AWS Regions and the AWS GovCloud (US) Regions where Amazon Keyspaces is offered. To learn more, see Logged batches in the Amazon Keyspaces Developer Guide.

title: Amazon RDS for Oracle now supports M8i and R8i instances with Oracle SE2 License Included
body: Amazon RDS for Oracle now offers M8i and R8i instances with Oracle Database Standard Edition 2 (SE2) with the License Included (LI). M8i and R8i instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors, available only on AWS, delivering the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. The new instances offer up to 15% better price-performance, and 2.5x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation Intel-based instances. With RDS for Oracle SE2 LI, customers don’t have to separately purchase Oracle license and support. Amazon RDS for Oracle SE2 LI offers subscription based pay-per-use pricing inclusive of software license, support, compute resources, and a managed database service. To use RDS for Oracle SE2 LI, customers can create database instances from the AWS Management Console or using the AWS CLI . and specify the LI option. For more details about how you can lower cost and simplify operations of running Oracle databases, refer to the AWS blog Rethink Oracle Standard Edition Two on Amazon RDS for Oracle . Configuration details for available instance types can be found on the Amazon RDS for Oracle Instance Types page. Review the AWS blog Rethink Oracle Standard Edition Two on Amazon RDS for Oracle to explore how you can lower cost and simplify operations by using Amazon RDS Oracle SE2 License Included instances for your Oracle databases. For pricing and AWS Region availability, see Amazon RDS for Oracle Pricing .
